newsitem.title: INDIA: Cricket-India loses both openers before lunch.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-India loses both openers before lunch.

text.p: India was 23 runs for the loss of two wickets in its second innings at lunch on the third day of the first test against South Africa.
The Indians who conceded a 21 run lead to the visitors on the first innings look to be in some trouble at this stage. India is ahead by two runs with eight wickets in hand.
Allan Donald sent back both the Indian openers in his opening spell. Sanjay Manjrekar was caught in the slips for five and Nayan Mongia was caught behind for an identical score.
At lunch, Rahul Dravid was batting on six in the company of skipper Sachin Tendulkar who had scored one.
Earlier South Africa, resuming at its overnight score of 202 for eight, was bowled out for 244 runs, a lead of 21 runs over the home side on the first innings.
Fanie De Villiers was unbeaten with 67 runs, the highest score of the match so far. He added sixty runs for the ninth wicket with fellow fast bowler Allan Donald.
The South African tail-enders who put on 125 runs for the last three wickets exposed the limitations of the Indian bowling attack on a pitch aiding spin.
The Indian spinners were unable to clear up the tail and it was left to paceman Javagal Srinath, bowling with the second new ball to finish off the South African innings.
Scores: India 223 and 23-2 at lunch. South Africa 244.
